title: Partition raw CDC batches by table and batch date; separate data and manifests

decision.date_basis: UTC date of the minimum payload.ts_ms within the original HTTP batch
decision.data_format: Original Debezium JSON envelope array, gzip compressed

rationale: Time-based partitioning and explicit key=value prefixes are documented storage patterns; the exact field names here are a project contract.
The lab has no measured need for two-character hash fanout. Readable table/date paths improve inspection and support bounded batch discovery.
Separate data and control prefixes prevent readers from treating receipt JSON as business events.
A date derived from batch contents remains stable across delayed retries. The receiver's current clock would send the same batch to a different partition after midnight.
Keep the original HTTP batch intact, including mixed-table batches. Their manifests enumerate all tables; table-specific consumers must include relevant _mixed batches.
Store the content hash in the filename to retain deterministic batch identities and byte-integrity checks. This does not provide event-level exactly-once processing.
limits: batch_date describes a batch's earliest capture date, not the business-event date or the source commit date. A batch can cross midnight; manifests retain both timestamp bounds.
The archived files remain small ingestion batches. Compaction into larger analytical files is a separate processing step and must preserve CDC order and deduplication semantics.
This convention is informed by enterprise practice; it is not a universal standard or a measured performance claim for SeaweedFS.
The project remains a single-VM lab without high availability or off-VM recovery validation.

migration.method: Pause capture, copy each verified batch without changing compressed or raw bytes, regenerate and verify manifests, reconcile coverage, then resume capture using existing offsets.
migration.rollback: Retain the complete v1 source archive, v1 image and source bundle. Reconcile any post-cutover v2 events before rolling back consumers or the writer; do not reset offsets.

sources.supports: Time-based partitioning, source/date examples, key=value paths and separate table hierarchies. AWS services are not used by this lab's data plane.
The Debezium SQL Server event envelope and the distinction between source timestamps and connector processing timestamps.
